proposal.blind_spot: The optimizer cannot tell whether a DRAM-hot streaming kernel is truly bandwidth-saturated (only byte removal helps) or latency/occupancy-limited (warps too few or stalled on global loads), because achieved occupancy and warp stall reasons are invisible.

rationale.sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustain: HIGH -> occupancy is fine; with dram% >= 90 declare the kernel at the bandwidth roofline: only remove bytes (fuse away materialized expand/contiguous copies) or, if traffic is irreducible, keep the simple kernel instead of regressing it / LOW -> raise residency: shrink BLOCK_SIZE, increase num_warps, cut register-heavy index math, or use grid-stride/persistent form to push dram% toward peak.
rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH with dram% 65-85% -> warps wait on global loads without filling the bus, add memory-level parallelism (more independent loads per thread, wider vectorized loads, num_stages/prefetch) / HIGH with dram% >= 90% -> bus is full, only traffic reduction helps / LOW -> global-load latency is not the limiter, stop restructuring the access pattern and leave the schedule unchanged.
